entries.title: Variety: mods, tuning, skills, new mechs and weapons
items: New pilots pick ONE maker's starter frame to begin with. Pilots who already have all four keep them.

Parts can carry mods that change how they work, not just their numbers: split barrels, wider blasts, cryo, void, fire and arc rounds, ricochets, gravity wells, cluster bomblets, burning ground, and more. Refined parts sometimes have one, Rare and better always do, and Experimental parts have two. The workshop can rewire a mod.
The parts dealer no longer sells Common parts. Rarer stock comes in as your rank rises, there's a featured Prototype-or-better part, and firmware chips are on the shelf. Crates drop rarer parts too.
A repair kit: press 1 (d-pad left, or Fix on a phone) to restore 30% of your armour, twice a mission. Upgrade it up to Mk V at the workshop.
Your starter frame comes with a firmware chip, and your first few crates always contain one. Every older pilot without a chip gets one now.

New in the hangar: the Tuning rig. Frame Tuning is four boards of upgrades with a choice of two big perks on rows 3 and 5, such as afterburner trails, phase dashes, shock landings, static shells and echo firing. You get 2 points a rank and 1 per story mission, and re-tuning is free.
Skills on key 2 (d-pad right): Repulsor Pulse, Arc Nova, Barrier Dome, Gravity Well, Decoy Holo, Cryo Burst, Orbital Lance and Overdrive, opening as you rank up.

8 new mechs, two per maker: Vantage, Rapier, Redoubt, Breaker, Bloom, Sickle, Hauler and Pogo. Wear 3 parts of one mech to switch on its set bonus. Breaker rams what you boost into, Bloom's repair kit heals teammates, and Redoubt braces when it stands still.

16 new weapons: a sweeping beam lance, a prism laser, an orbital lance, a wave scythe, a gravity well launcher, a cryo projector, an arc coil, seeker orbs, a storm caller, a nanite sprayer, a returning saw disc, and more. Cryo freezes enemies; void ignores armour.
City missions now come in 7 new layouts besides the grid: canal quarter, ring plaza, city park, old town, rail yard, harbour front and megablocks.
Maker reputation and licences are gone.
Fixed: holding a shield while getting hit could stop the mission. Closing a bay with Esc no longer opens the hangar menu. A Prototype shield showed blocking over 100%.

entries.title: The Outskirts
items: A second region past the city: the Outskirts. Switch between Larkspur and the Outskirts with the tabs above the campaign map.
Pinewatch Ridge — daylight pine forest with a river, a hydro dam and a logging camp. Open from the start: its story mission and contracts are waiting.
Red Mesa — red desert badlands with mesas, a wind farm, a solar field and a Halden-Voss forward base. Free Pinewatch to reach it.
Frostline — a snowfield in the mountains with a radar station, a ski lift and a frozen lake. The ice is slippery: frames slide on it. Free Red Mesa to reach it.
Contracts come up in every area you've reached, so you'll see outdoor maps on the board between city jobs.

entries.title: Overload, the walker, the moon and versus
items: Overload cores: three late generators you can craft from rank 6. Deal damage to fill the bar, then press V (d-pad down, or the Overload button on a phone). Surge fires faster with no heat, Bastion shrugs off most damage and shelters teammates, Cascade blasts everything around you.

A second boss: the Juggernaut, a Halden-Voss siege walker. Break its shield generator from behind, then its cannon, missile racks and legs. Every attack is marked on the ground first. It drops siege plate. Find it in Iron Stride, in the Kettle, after Sawtooth.

New enemies: flamer troopers, shield projectors that protect the army inside their dome, medic drones that repair it, spore drifters whose gas slows you down, and Halden-Voss line frames — enemy mechs that fly like aces.
The moon: Quiet Dust takes you to a mining outpost on the moon. Low gravity means huge jumps, long hovers and quick boosts that slide. It opens from the Crown once the Broodmother is down.

Long missions: The Long Night (in the Spindle) comes in three parts with a checkpoint after each. Lose, and you can fly it again from the last checkpoint with everything you'd picked up — alone or with your co-op room.
The Proving Ground (in the Foundry, after Sawtooth): five arena rounds against Halden-Voss frames, then their aces.
Versus: in a co-op room, the host can pick Crossfire (red against blue) or Scrapyard Brawl (every frame for itself). First to three rounds wins. Bots can fill the sides.
On phones, a boss's parts now show as one slim row of pips instead of three rows of names.

Every objective now shows where it is: an arrow at the edge of the screen to each target (with its distance), a beam on targets in view, a minimap on wide screens, and a full mission map (Tab or M, the View button, or the Map button).
Hold the Line is now a four-minute hold instead of nine, with the waves packed closer together.

entries.title: Online co-op
items: Co-op is here: fly any mission with up to three friends. Open Co-op from the title screen or the hangar menu, host a room, and send the four-letter code, the link or the QR code.
Friends can join in the middle of a mission and land right beside you. If someone's connection drops, a bot flies their frame until they're back (up to 90 seconds).
Everyone brings their own frame and keeps their own loot, rolled at their own rank. The pay is never split: everyone gets all of it.
Enemies get tougher and there are more of them for each extra frame in the team.
Bots: fill empty seats with bot pilots, or bring up to three of them on a solo mission from the briefing. They stick with you, fight, revive you and plant charges.
When a teammate goes down, stand next to them: a ring fills, and they're back up. Press C (d-pad up) to ping a spot or an enemy for the team.
Rooms can be Invite only or Public; public rooms show up under Find a game. The host can remove someone, and everyone else can vote to.
Pick your callsign on the Co-op screen; teammates see it over your frame.
Fixed: the header bar on the contracts board was squashed so its Back button overlapped the page.
Once a mission's job is done, a green arrow at the edge of the screen points to the dropship (with how far it is), and a beam marks the pad.
Fixed: Report a bug could get stuck on "Sending…". It now always finishes, and a report that can't be sent waits on your device and goes later.

entries.title: The hangar and the city campaign
items: The hangar is open: walk your frame around it and step into a bay to use it. There's an assembly bay, a parts dealer, a workshop, a paint bay, a test range and the launch pad.

Every part you pick up is now a real part with a rarity (Common to Experimental) and bonus lines. Grade A and S missions give crates with more parts, materials, and sometimes firmware chips or secret recipes.

Assembly bay: change any part or weapon, and see how each swap changes your armour, speed, energy and the rest before you fit it. Save up to eight builds. All four makers' starter frames are already yours.
Firmware chips go in your CPU: more crit chance, faster locks, more energy, or a two-handed weapon held in one arm.
Workshop: build parts you've seen, re-roll a bonus, raise a part's rarity, burn chips, or scrap parts you don't need. Secret recipes for odd weapons turn up as schematics in crates.
Paint bay: 16 paint schemes (more unlock as your rank rises) or your own colours, kept per build.
Test range: try your build on target dummies, with damage per second on screen.
Pilot rank: missions earn experience. Higher ranks bring better parts to the dealer and unlock recipes.

The campaign: free the city of Larkspur one district at a time. The map lights back up as you go. Four new story missions: stop a truck convoy, plant charges on relay masts, escort evacuation trucks, and a drop from orbit where you steer your own landing.
A rival ace: Sawtooth, a Halden-Voss pilot in her own frame, who boosts, dodges and overheats just like you. Two more rival pilots are waiting later in the campaign.

The first boss: the Broodmother. Burst her egg sacs and break her claws to open her armoured head. Her claw sweeps, charges and spit always show on the ground before they land. Broken parts drop chitin, a new boss material.
Contracts: new jobs appear in every district you can reach, refreshed after each mission: clear-outs, nest burns, demolition, hunts, sabotage, data-core recovery, convoy raids and escorts.
Maker licences: contracts earn a maker's trust. Licences put more of their parts on the dealer's shelves, even above your rank, at a discount.
Signed in, your pilot is saved to your account. If two devices disagree, you choose which save to keep, and the other is kept so you can swap back from Settings.

entries.title: Overdrive Frame is here
items: Pick one of four makers' frames and drop into a neon city to take contracts: clear a swarm-filled district, burn a rival company's tank farms, or hold the line while the last evacuation trains leave.
Your frame boosts, quick-boosts sideways, jumps onto rooftops and hovers. Boosting and firing use energy and build heat, so watch the two arcs around your mech.
Hundreds of enemies at once: swarms that pour in along the streets, leapers, acid spitters and armoured brutes you have to get behind, plus troopers, tanks, rocket artillery and gunships.
Buildings break apart as they take damage, burn, and collapse onto whatever is next to them. Fuel tanks blow up.
Every mission ends with a grade from S to D that sets your pay. Losing never costs your frame; you keep what you picked up.
